heading: INT. HARROWGATE MUSEUM OF NATURAL CURIOSITIES - TAXIDERMY HALL - NIGHT

units.text: INT. HARROWGATE MUSEUM OF NATURAL CURIOSITIES - TAXIDERMY HALL - NIGHT
Glass cases in rows, and in every case a creature caught in the middle of a thought: a fox mid-pounce, an owl with one wing half raised, a stoat frozen beside a nest of china eggs.
The gaslamps hiss.
The floor smells of beeswax and arsenic.

PROFESSOR ALDOUS BLYTHE, 60s, in a velvet jacket and a monocle, strolls along the cases with a candle, humming, while ROSALIND PEMBERTON-SHAW, 30s, the junior curator, trails him with a notebook, writing and sneezing, and CONSTABLE HARGROVE, 40s, a heavy man in a cape, stands with his hands behind his back, studying a stuffed heron as though it has insulted him.
You see, Constable, the trick of the thing is not the skin. It is the eyes.
units.name: BLYTHE

units.text: Glass, ain't they?
units.name: HARGROVE

units.text: Glass, certainly. But placed by a hand that knew the animal.
units.name: BLYTHE

units.text: Professor, with respect, the Constable is here about the missing curator.
units.name: ROSALIND

units.text: Ah, yes. Dear Mr. Fitch. He did so love the badgers.
units.name: BLYTHE

units.text: Last seen Thursday?
units.name: HARGROVE

units.text: Thursday evening. Closing time. He went down to oil the hinges on the Great Elk.
units.name: BLYTHE

units.text: The three of them turn toward the end of the hall.
The Great Elk stands in its alcove, antlers spread like a cathedral window, glass eyes catching the candle.
Something shifts behind the elk.
ARCHIBALD FITCH, 50s, in a rumpled waistcoat, steps from behind the elk, alive, pale, holding an oil can.
He looks at them like a man waking from a dream.
I fell asleep.
units.name: FITCH

units.text: Silence.
Mr. Fitch! We thought you were dead!
units.name: ROSALIND

units.text: For four days?
units.name: FITCH

units.text: Well. It was a very long afternoon.
units.name: BLYTHE

units.text: Hargrove frowns.
He looks at the elk.
At Fitch.
At Blythe, whose candle has begun to shake.
Professor. There's a piece of tweed in that elk's antlers.
units.name: HARGROVE

units.text: Everyone looks up.
A scrap of grey cloth.
Wet, dark at one end.
That is... decorative.
units.name: BLYTHE
